economicFacts.fact: Lowering average equity exposure lowers drawdown and CAGR together; in every US/KR overlay measured so far the return gap to passive is almost all LEVEL, not TIMING.
The equity effect of FOMC shocks is priced within the shock month; MP vs information origin does not change 1-12 month subsequent returns.
Information-type FOMC shocks are followed by persistently higher real yields and lower breakevens (6-12 months), not by EBP moves.
The relation between credit stress and 12-month large losses flipped around 1990 (0-15% loss frequency 1970-89 vs 12-69% 1990-2024).
Trend/volatility information modestly beats the base rate for 6-month loss probability (+4.6% Brier skill, 1990-2024).
Fast volatility is the clearest descriptive link to near-term KR downside; curve re-steepening after inversion matters more than inversion.
The existing FAST trend/volatility model was 'normal' at some month-end in the 126 sessions before each of the 7 US -15% first passages since 1993.
Real-time BAA and GS10 vintages exist from 1996-12-03; month-end as-of credit is available 1996-12..2026-10 with a ~2-month observation lag.

openCompetingExplanations: Credit stress is coincident with, not ahead of, equity breaks (both respond to the same news); P1 tests the lead directly.
Any credit lead is regime-specific (post-1990 credit-driven crises) and will not persist (Goyal-Welch instability).
Drawdown onsets are dominated by fast exogenous shocks (2020, 2025) that no monthly macro signal can lead.
Monthly-average credit with a ~2-month publication lag is too slow for 126-session onsets; daily PIT credit is unavailable before 2014.
